citation: Reproduces Cont, R. and Schaanning, E. (2017), Fire sales, indirect contagion and systemic stress testing.

dedupe_keys.name: firesale stresstest agent based model of fire sale contagion among eu banks

description: firesale_stresstest is an agent-based model of fire-sale contagion among systemically important EU banks, in which banks hold tradable assets, face leverage constraints and sell assets to avoid default, and the sales depress prices through market price impact functions and so spread losses to other holders. It is published by the Oxford Institute for New Economic Thinking (INET) complexity economics group as a Python 3 hybrid Jupyter notebook that reproduces the results of Cont and Schaanning (2017) on fire sales and indirect contagion in systemic stress testing. The data are the bank-level results of the European Banking Authority's 2018 EU-wide stress test, so coverage is the EU banking sector at that date. The code is free under the Apache 2.0 licence. Caveats: the repository shows no recent releases, so it is marked stale, the balance sheets are frozen at 2018, and price impact parameters are assumptions that drive results. For simulation it is a ready example of cascading failure through overlapping portfolios, showing how a shock to some banks, which could come from infrastructure or disaster losses, spreads through markets. It is related to the resilience library record in this catalogue, the same group's general framework, and to the EBA EU-wide stress testing record, which supplies its input data.
